title: What drives people to  extremism? With Arie Kruglanski, PhD, and Sophia Moskalenko, PhD

sentences.en: What does it mean to be an extremist?
sentences.zh: 什么是极端主义？

sentences.en: The word might call up images of political violence or terrorism, but extreme behaviors are all around us and can be a force for good as well as destruction.
sentences.zh: 这个词可能会让人联想到政治暴力或恐怖主义，但极端行为其实无处不在，它既可以是破坏性的力量，也可以是向善的力量。

sentences.en: Extreme single-mindedness and focus can spur scientists to make new discoveries and artists to create great art.
sentences.zh: 极端的专注和执着可以激励科学家做出新发现，也能让艺术家创作出伟大的艺术作品。

sentences.en: Today we're going to talk to two psychologists about the psychology of the extreme.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与两位心理学家探讨极端心理学。

sentences.en: What drives people to extreme behaviors, both constructive and destructive?
sentences.zh: 是什么驱使人们做出建设性或破坏性的极端行为？

sentences.en: Is there an extremist personality?
sentences.zh: 是否存在“极端主义人格”？

sentences.en: And if so, is it something you're born with?
sentences.zh: 如果有，它是与生俱来的吗？

sentences.en: Is there a connection between extremism and mental illness?
sentences.zh: 极端主义与精神疾病之间有联系吗？

sentences.en: How does social media drive extremism?
sentences.zh: 社交媒体是如何助长极端主义的？

sentences.en: Is the world becoming more extreme?
sentences.zh: 世界是否正变得越来越极端？

sentences.en: And can psychological research on extremism suggest ways to reach people at risk of turning violent or harming others?
sentences.zh: 关于极端主义的心理学研究，能否为接触那些有暴力倾向或伤害他人风险的人提供建议？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》。

sentences.en: The flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: I have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 今天我有两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: First is Dr. Ari Kruglansky, a distinguished professor of psychology at the University of Maryland and a founding co-director and co-principal investigator of NC START,
sentences.zh: 第一位是马里兰大学心理学杰出教授、NC START的创始联合主任兼联合首席研究员阿里·克鲁格兰斯基博士，

sentences.en: the National Center for the Study of Terrorism and the Response to Terrorism.
sentences.zh: NC START即国家恐怖主义研究与应对恐怖主义中心。

sentences.en: His research interests include violent extremism, political activism, the quest for significance, and closed-mindedness.
sentences.zh: 他的研究兴趣包括暴力极端主义、政治激进主义、对意义的追求以及封闭心态。

sentences.en: Dr. Kruglansky is the author of more than 400 academic articles, chapters, and books.
sentences.zh: 克鲁格兰斯基博士撰写了400多篇学术文章、章节和书籍。

sentences.en: He has won many awards for his work, including APA's 2025 Award for Distinguished Scientific Contributions.
sentences.zh: 他因其工作获得了许多奖项，包括美国心理学会2025年杰出科学贡献奖。

sentences.en: Next is Dr. Sofia Moskalenko, a research fellow at Georgia State University and a program management specialist at the UN Office of Counterterrorism Behavioral Insights Hub.
sentences.zh: 下一位是佐治亚州立大学研究员、联合国反恐办公室行为洞察中心项目管理专家索菲亚·莫斯卡连科博士。

sentences.en: She's a social and clinical psychologist who studies extremism, terrorism, and radicalization, and was previously a researcher at NC START.
sentences.zh: 她是一位社会和临床心理学家，研究极端主义、恐怖主义和激进化，此前曾是NC START的研究员。

sentences.en: Dr. Moskalenko and Dr. Kruglansky are co-authors of a new book called The Psychology of the Extreme, which was published in February.
sentences.zh: 莫斯卡连科博士和克鲁格兰斯基博士合著了一本新书《极端心理学》，该书于二月出版。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining me.
sentences.zh: 感谢两位参加我的节目。

sentences.en: Pleased to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: For both of you, much of your work has focused on political extremism and violence, but in your new book, you talk about extremism more broadly.
sentences.zh: 对你们两位来说，你们的大部分工作都集中在政治极端主义和暴力上，但在新书中，你们更广泛地讨论了极端主义。

sentences.en: So let me ask you, how do you define extremism?
sentences.zh: 那么请问，你们如何定义极端主义？

sentences.en: Extremism is a psychological state of motivational imbalance that happens when one of our basic needs
sentences.zh: 极端主义是一种动机失衡的心理状态，当我们的某种基本需求变得如此主导，

sentences.en: is so dominant that it crowds out the others, and when that happens, the constraints that those other needs normally impose on behavior are relaxed, if not completely removed.
sentences.zh: 以至于排挤了其他需求时，就会发生这种情况。一旦发生，其他需求通常对行为施加的约束就会被放松，甚至完全消除。

sentences.en: And when that happens, anything that serves that dominant need is legitimized, is permitted, including things that would otherwise be constrained by alternative considerations.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，任何服务于该主导需求的行为都会被合法化、被允许，包括那些本应受到其他考量约束的行为。

sentences.en: So take, for example, hunger.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，饥饿。

sentences.en: When we are moderately hungry, our eating behavior is constrained by considerations of health, of
sentences.zh: 当我们适度饥饿时，我们的进食行为会受到健康、

sentences.en: taste, of social norms, of what people in our society consider as legitimate for consumption.
sentences.zh: 口味、社会规范以及社会认为何种食物适合消费等因素的约束。

sentences.en: But when the hunger becomes extreme, all those constraints fade away, and anything is legitimized
sentences.zh: 但当饥饿变得极端时，所有这些约束都会消失，任何东西都会被合法化，

sentences.en: for consumption, including bark of the trees, your pets, even bodies of other human beings, as was demonstrated in this unfortunate, tragic event in the Andes, when a plane crashed
sentences.zh: 包括树皮、宠物，甚至是其他人的尸体，正如安第斯山脉那场不幸的悲剧事件所证明的那样，当时飞机坠毁，

sentences.en: and the survivors were forced to eat their fallen comrades' flesh.
sentences.zh: 幸存者被迫吃掉已故同伴的肉。

sentences.en: So this paradigm of removal of constraints is something that applies to extremism across the board.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种消除约束的范式适用于各领域的极端主义。

sentences.en: So, for example, when the need for significance and mattering is the predominant need, considerations of life, family, career, social norms fade away, and you do anything.
sentences.zh: 例如，当对意义和重要性的需求成为主导需求时，对生命、家庭、事业、社会规范的考量就会消失，你会不顾一切。

sentences.en: You would kill and die in order to satisfy that need.
sentences.zh: 为了满足那种需求，你会杀人，也会去死。

sentences.en: And that's, you know, the paradigmatic instance of extremism, this motivational imbalance, this one-track mind that legitimizes anything that serves that dominant need.
sentences.zh: 这就是极端主义的典型范例，这种动机失衡，这种让任何服务于主导需求的行为都合法化的“单行道”思维。

sentences.en: So that sounds like we all have the potential for extremism, but there must be some factors that are happening psychologically that prevent us from doing this all the time.
sentences.zh: 听起来我们每个人都有极端主义的潜能，但心理上一定有一些因素阻止我们一直这样做。

sentences.en: Is that correct?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: So, as Ari already indicated in his response, we believe that extremism is a biologically built-in
sentences.zh: 正如阿里在回答中指出的那样，我们认为极端主义是一种生物内置的机制，

sentences.en: mechanism that humans evolved to have in order to overcome situations of crises, situations
sentences.zh: 人类进化出这种机制是为了克服危机情况，

sentences.en: where it's life or death, and you're in the desert and you need water, or you're being chased by a predator or enemies.
sentences.zh: 比如生死关头，你在沙漠中需要水，或者被捕食者或敌人追赶。

sentences.en: And in those situations, you can't be distracted by other things.
sentences.zh: 在那种情况下，你不能被其他事情分心。

sentences.en: You have to mobilize the entire repertoire of your resources and abilities to deal with the crisis.
sentences.zh: 你必须调动所有的资源和能力来应对危机。

sentences.en: And so when we think about extremism outside of our primordial environments, all it takes sometimes is to get a person into the mindset that this is life or death,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们思考原始环境之外的极端主义时，有时只需要让人进入一种“生死攸关”的心态，

sentences.en: that this is their existential need, you know?
sentences.zh: 认为这是他们的生存需求，你懂吗？

sentences.en: And it's not so hard to do.
sentences.zh: 这并不难做到。

sentences.en: We're pretty good at creating narratives that are convincing of that.
sentences.zh: 我们非常擅长编造令人信服的叙事。

sentences.en: And possibly in today's world, there are people who are especially adept at doing that.
sentences.zh: 在当今世界，可能有些人特别擅长这一点。

sentences.en: You know, we know about the evening news.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们都知道晚间新闻。

sentences.en: They want to keep you on because they show you these shocking and horrible things.
sentences.zh: 他们想让你留下来，因为他们会展示那些令人震惊和恐怖的事情。

sentences.en: But also, everyday exposure to news online is prioritizing things that are shocking, that are disturbing, because it multiplies user engagement, which is what a lot of social media
sentences.zh: 此外，日常在线接触的新闻也会优先考虑那些令人震惊、不安的内容，因为这能成倍增加用户参与度，而这正是许多社交媒体所追求的。

sentences.en: are after.
sentences.zh: （接上句）

sentences.en: So this mindset of survival and crisis that breeds extremism is not only limited to what extremism was originally designed for, it's been co-opted and is very widely used today
sentences.zh: 因此，这种滋生极端主义的生存和危机心态，不仅限于极端主义最初的设计目的，它现在已被广泛利用，用来获取人们的注意力，并让他们进入这种极端心态，无论是为了在线购物，还是为了加入某些在线极端社区，

sentences.en: to harvest people's attention and to get them into this extremist mindset, whether it's buying things online or, you know, getting into some extremist communities online that have
sentences.zh: （接上句）

sentences.en: to do with eating in a particular way or like starving themselves or bodybuilding or indeed getting engaged with radical political ideas and actions.
sentences.zh: 这些社区可能与特定的饮食方式有关，比如节食、健美，或者确实是参与激进的政治思想和行动。

sentences.en: In the beginning of the book, you give examples of two people we might not think of together, but who both typify extremism in different ways.
sentences.zh: 在书的开头，你们举了两个我们可能不会联想到一起的人的例子，但他们都以不同的方式代表了极端主义。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking of Gandhi and bin Laden.
sentences.zh: 我想到的是甘地和本·拉登。

sentences.en: Can you tell us about that?
sentences.zh: 能跟我们谈谈吗？

sentences.en: What traits do these vastly dissimilar people share?
sentences.zh: 这些截然不同的人有什么共同特征？

sentences.en: I'm going to just briefly talk about it because Sophia is an expert on both.
sentences.zh: 我简单说一下，因为索菲亚是这两方面的专家。

sentences.en: But I think that what is common to them is the single-mindedness and their readiness to sacrifice anything that falls outside the domain of that particular need.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们的共同点是那种专注力，以及为了满足特定需求而牺牲一切的准备。

sentences.en: So in both cases, the underlying need was the quest for significance for their nation, for their religion.
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下，潜在的需求都是为他们的国家、为他们的宗教寻求意义。

sentences.en: And that justified a variety of practices that one would call extreme rejection of all
sentences.zh: 这证明了各种被称为极端的做法是合理的：对甘地而言是拒绝所有西方的行事方式，

sentences.en: Western modes of doing things for Gandhi, the mobilization of people, believers to fight the West, to fight and kill non-believers by Al-Qaeda.
sentences.zh: 对基地组织而言是动员信徒对抗西方，去战斗并杀死非信徒。

sentences.en: That single-mindedness, that one-track mind, readiness to sacrifice all on the altar of that need was what common to both.
sentences.zh: 那种专注，那种“单行道”思维，为了满足需求而牺牲一切的准备，是他们共同的特点。

sentences.en: But Sophia can add to that because she studied Gandhi and Osama extensively.
sentences.zh: 但索菲亚可以补充，因为她深入研究过甘地和奥萨马。

sentences.en: So they also share some biographical information that is maybe strange to those of us who only know them as these giants in the political and historical landscape.
sentences.zh: 他们确实还有一些生平信息，对于那些只把他们视为政治和历史巨头的人来说，可能显得有些奇怪。

sentences.en: So they both grew up in quite prominent and well-to-do families.
sentences.zh: 他们都成长在相当显赫和富裕的家庭中。

sentences.en: They both were very shy when they were young, not known as leaders among their peers at all, kind of staying outside of the struggle for significance, at least at that moment.
sentences.zh: 他们年轻时都很害羞，在同龄人中根本不是领袖，至少在那一刻，他们游离于对意义的争夺之外。

sentences.en: However, at a certain point in their late teens, they both became increasingly interested
sentences.zh: 然而，在十几岁末期，他们都开始对反殖民斗争产生浓厚兴趣，

sentences.en: in what was essentially, for both of them, an anti-colonial struggle because they both grew
sentences.zh: 因为他们都成长在被殖民大国统治的国家，并认为这是不公正的，需要解决。

sentences.en: up in countries that were dominated by a colonial power and felt that that was unjust and it needs to be addressed.
sentences.zh: （接上句）

sentences.en: And so both of them started first changing their diet, which is something we find across a lot of cases of extremism.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们两人都开始改变饮食习惯，我们在许多极端主义案例中都发现了这一点。

sentences.en: That may be, you know, the first thing you notice about somebody is they change how they eat.
sentences.zh: 这可能是你注意到某人变化的第一件事：他们改变了饮食方式。

sentences.en: For Osama bin Laden, that was that he'd begun fasting two days a week like the prophet, which for a teenage boy is a huge commitment.
sentences.zh: 对于奥萨马·本·拉登来说，他开始像先知一样每周禁食两天，这对一个十几岁的男孩来说是一个巨大的承诺。

sentences.en: Fasting is like not eating at all, right?
sentences.zh: 禁食就是完全不吃东西，对吧？

sentences.en: For two days a week.
sentences.zh: 每周两天。

sentences.en: And he started doing it himself.
sentences.zh: 他开始自己这样做。

sentences.en: And then he started pushing his family, his mother and his stepmother and his step siblings to follow him on this path.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始推动他的家人，他的母亲、继母和继兄弟姐妹也走上这条路。

sentences.en: For Gandhi, it was his vow to remain vegetarian, even though he was studying in London.
sentences.zh: 对于甘地来说，是他发誓要保持素食，尽管当时他在伦敦学习。

sentences.en: And in London at that time, it was very difficult to be vegetarian and still eat in a way that he enjoyed.
sentences.zh: 在当时的伦敦，要保持素食同时还能吃到自己喜欢的食物非常困难。

sentences.en: So really serious self-sacrifices in order to maintain and cultivate what they felt was important to them politically and as far as their identity was concerned.
sentences.zh: 所以，为了维持和培养他们认为在政治上和身份认同上重要的事情，他们确实做出了严重的自我牺牲。

sentences.en: And then these sacrifices only grew greater.
sentences.zh: 而且这些牺牲只会越来越大。

sentences.en: You know, they started giving up the way they looked to others.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们开始放弃自己在他人眼中的形象。

sentences.en: And as a result, they stood out with their dress.
sentences.zh: 结果，他们的着装变得与众不同。

sentences.en: Gandhi gave up on the Western clothes.
sentences.zh: 甘地放弃了西式服装。

sentences.en: Osama bin Laden started to wear traditional Muslim clothes and kind of felt that people who didn't do it were not right.
sentences.zh: 奥萨马·本·拉登开始穿传统的穆斯林服装，并觉得不这样做的人是不对的。

sentences.en: Friends that were dressing in shorts, for example, to play soccer were violating a moral boundary.
sentences.zh: 例如，穿短裤踢足球的朋友就触犯了道德界限。

sentences.en: And Osama bin Laden expressed it to his friends.
sentences.zh: 奥萨马·本·拉登向他的朋友表达了这一点。

sentences.en: So this dynamic process of, on the one hand, breaking social norms in order to cultivate a particular belief.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个动态过程：一方面，为了培养某种特定的信仰而打破社会规范；

sentences.en: And on the other hand, with that, breaking or straining social relationships, because that's what happens when an extremist begins that extremist journey.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，随之而来的是打破或疏远社会关系，因为当极端分子开始那段极端之旅时，就会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: Other people feel the changes in them.
sentences.zh: 其他人能感觉到他们的变化。

sentences.en: And sometimes the extremist will express to them the desire that they follow them or change their own behaviors.
sentences.zh: 有时极端分子会向他们表达希望他们跟随自己或改变行为的愿望。

sentences.en: That's strange social relationships.
sentences.zh: 这会使社会关系变得紧张。

sentences.en: So what happened in both Osama bin Laden's and Gandhi's trajectory to becoming who they became as we knew them is some serious isolation.
sentences.zh: 所以，奥萨马·本·拉登和甘地在成为我们所熟知的人的过程中，都经历了一些严重的孤立。

sentences.en: And for Gandhi, that was pivotal.
sentences.zh: 对甘地来说，这是关键。

sentences.en: So he was in South Africa about to travel on the train.
sentences.zh: 当时他在南非，正准备坐火车。

sentences.en: He was already feeling as a discriminated minority being an Indian in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 作为南非的印度人，他已经感到自己是受歧视的少数群体。

sentences.en: And he had a first class ticket, but he was rejected from first class because he was an Indian.
sentences.zh: 他有一张头等舱车票，但因为他是印度人，被拒绝进入头等舱。

sentences.en: So given a choice of going to the second class or disembarking the train, he chose the latter.
sentences.zh: 在选择去二等舱还是下车之间，他选择了后者。

sentences.en: And he ended up spending a night on the platform all alone following this grave injustice.
sentences.zh: 在那次严重的非正义事件后，他独自在站台上过了一夜。

sentences.en: And that's when he came up with the idea of satyagraha, which is the idea of peaceful,
sentences.zh: 就在那时，他想出了“萨蒂亚格拉哈”（Satyagraha）的想法，即和平、

sentences.en: nonviolent resistance that then became the signature of his life and the movement that followed him.
sentences.zh: 非暴力抵抗的理念，这后来成为了他一生的标志，也成为了追随他的运动的标志。

sentences.en: For Osama bin Laden, the isolation was the result of his increased radicalization and his growing conflict with governments, including his own government, the Saudi government,
sentences.zh: 对于奥萨马·本·拉登来说，孤立是他日益激进化以及与各国政府（包括他自己的政府，沙特政府）冲突加剧的结果，

sentences.en: and him becoming a persona non grata and somebody who was hunted internationally.
sentences.zh: 他成为了不受欢迎的人，并遭到国际通缉。

sentences.en: And the isolation and secrecy that that kind of life entailed also brought him into seclusion.
sentences.zh: 那种生活所带来的孤立和秘密也让他陷入了隐居。

sentences.en: And that's another hallmark of an extremist's journey, that at some point they end up quite isolated.
sentences.zh: 这也是极端分子旅程的另一个标志，即在某个时刻，他们最终变得相当孤立。

sentences.en: And the only people who can stand their demands and their extremism are other extremists.
sentences.zh: 而唯一能忍受他们的要求和极端主义的人，就是其他极端分子。

sentences.en: And that very often, like it was for Gandhi, is the kind of moment that pushes them ultimate lifestyle and choice that defines their extremist and themselves.
sentences.zh: 这通常就像甘地那样，是一个推动他们最终选择定义其极端主义和他们自身的生活方式的时刻。

sentences.en: I wanted to add something to that, and that is that there is many more followers and imitators of Osama bin Laden than there are of Gandhi.
sentences.zh: 我想补充一点，那就是奥萨马·本·拉登的追随者和模仿者比甘地的要多得多。

sentences.en: And there is a good reason for it, in the sense that the violent way of attaining significance through aggression, through dominance, through the glory of militancy,
sentences.zh: 这有充分的理由，因为通过侵略、统治、好战的荣耀来获得意义的暴力方式，

sentences.en: is a very primordial way of attaining significance.
sentences.zh: 是一种非常原始的获得意义的方式。

sentences.en: Whereas the more passive resistance that Gandhi advocated is much less direct assertion of your power, of your dominance, of your mattering.
sentences.zh: 而甘地所倡导的更被动的抵抗，则远没有那么直接地宣示你的力量、你的统治地位和你的重要性。

sentences.en: So I think that's one difference between these two, who share many commonalities.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是这两个有很多共同点的人之间的一个区别。

sentences.en: And one commonality that Sophia didn't mention is that both of them were assassinated for their ideology.
sentences.zh: 索菲亚没有提到的一个共同点是，他们两人都因为自己的意识形态而被暗杀。

sentences.en: You describe personality traits that sound very much like fixations of the type that you might see in somebody who has maybe autism spectrum disorder or obsessive compulsive disorder.
sentences.zh: 你描述的性格特征听起来非常像你在患有自闭症谱系障碍或强迫症的人身上可能看到的固着行为。

sentences.en: And I'm just wondering whether extremism is related to these kinds of mental health disorders.
sentences.zh: 我只是想知道极端主义是否与这些心理健康障碍有关。

sentences.en: So I don't know that I would put it that way, that most people who are exhibiting extremist tendencies are not diagnosable as having any kind of mental health issues.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我会那样说，因为大多数表现出极端倾向的人，并不能被诊断为患有任何心理健康问题。

sentences.en: And in fact, as we started saying, extremism is in everybody's repertoire and under the right conditions, everybody will probably act in an extreme way.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正如我们开始所说，极端主义存在于每个人的潜能中，在适当的条件下，每个人都可能以极端的方式行事。

sentences.en: So in that sense, it's a normative possibility to be extreme.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，变得极端是一种规范的可能性。

sentences.en: However, mental illness often looks very much like extremism in the singular obsession with something.
sentences.zh: 然而，精神疾病看起来确实很像极端主义，表现为对某件事的单一痴迷。

sentences.en: So for anorexics, it's the obsession with losing weight and restraining their calorie intake.
sentences.zh: 对于厌食症患者来说，是对减肥和限制卡路里摄入的痴迷。

sentences.en: For people who have obsessive compulsive disorder, it's whatever the fear is.
sentences.zh: 对于患有强迫症的人来说，无论恐惧是什么，

sentences.en: Maybe it's the fear of germs or fear of being trampled that becomes the singular obsession that ends up defining much of their day-to-day lives and their behaviors.
sentences.zh: 也许是对细菌的恐惧，或者是对被踩踏的恐惧，这成为了单一的痴迷，最终定义了他们大部分的日常生活和行为。

sentences.en: Some forms of depression,
sentences.zh: 某些形式的抑郁症，

sentences.en: they have this feature of rumination where a person spends much of their time just thinking back about all the failures that they've experienced and all the things that they think are wrong with them and rejections and so on.
sentences.zh: 它们具有反刍思维的特征，一个人大部分时间都在回想他们经历过的所有失败，所有他们认为自己做错的事情，以及拒绝等等。

sentences.en: And this circular, endless loop of negative thought ends up consuming them to the degree that it becomes a mental health issue.
sentences.zh: 这种循环往复、无休止的负面思维最终消耗了他们，以至于变成了心理健康问题。

sentences.en: So mental disorders are disordered ways of thinking, of feeling, of behaving that can look very much like extremism, which at some points can be very normative.
sentences.zh: 所以精神障碍是思维、感觉、行为的紊乱方式，看起来非常像极端主义，而极端主义在某些时候可能是非常规范的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, again, you know, the manifestation has this common element of fixating on one thing to the exclusion of other things.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，再次强调，这种表现形式有一个共同点，即专注于一件事而排斥其他事情。

sentences.en: The etiology could be different.
sentences.zh: 病因可能不同。

sentences.en: For example, in the case of autism, it's unclear that what is happening is suppression of other things or simply those other things not being particularly well developed,
sentences.zh: 例如，在自闭症的情况下，不清楚发生的是对其他事物的抑制，还是仅仅是那些事物没有得到特别好的发展，

sentences.en: like social sensitivity and, you know, social awareness.
sentences.zh: 比如社交敏感性和社交意识。

sentences.en: And so it may look similarly on the surface and yet have different underlying etiology.
sentences.zh: 所以表面上看起来可能相似，但潜在的病因却不同。

sentences.en: It's a fascinating possibility to look at the commonalities and how far, how deeply they go into the psychological process.
sentences.zh: 研究这些共同点以及它们在心理过程中深入到什么程度，是一个迷人的可能性。

sentences.en: And that's something that future generations of researchers hopefully will pursue.
sentences.zh: 这是未来几代研究人员希望能够追求的方向。

sentences.en: Is it just my impression or is the world becoming more extremist?
sentences.zh: 是我的错觉，还是世界正变得越来越极端？

sentences.en: Do we go through cycles in history where there are times when things are more extreme and less extreme?
sentences.zh: 我们是否在历史中经历周期，有时事情更极端，有时不那么极端？

sentences.en: I think that the world is becoming more extreme, to some extent, driven by the technology of social media and the Internet.
sentences.zh: 我认为世界正在变得越来越极端，在某种程度上是由社交媒体和互联网技术驱动的。

sentences.en: You know, the clamor, the competition for attention, the competition for being popular and acceptable drives this idea of standing out, mattering, being somebody to huge extremes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对注意力的争夺，对受欢迎和被接受的竞争，将这种脱颖而出、变得重要、成为某人的想法推向了巨大的极端。

sentences.en: I just read a story yesterday in Washington Post about a ski jumper who jumped to his death in order to attain the glory of doing something that would make his video viral.
sentences.zh: 我昨天刚在《华盛顿邮报》上读到一个故事，关于一名跳台滑雪运动员跳向死亡，为了获得做某事让视频疯传的荣耀。

sentences.en: And so that kind of competition for attention that is propagated by the social media is instilling proclivity to go to the extremes in order to stand out, in order to matter,
sentences.zh: 因此，社交媒体传播的这种对注意力的竞争，正在灌输一种走向极端的倾向，为了脱颖而出，为了变得重要，

sentences.en: in order to have significance, have the attention of other people.
sentences.zh: 为了拥有意义，拥有其他人的关注。

sentences.en: Sofia, you want to add to that?
sentences.zh: 索菲亚，你想补充吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's my impression, too, that the world is becoming more extreme.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的印象也是世界正在变得越来越极端。

sentences.en: I think that the social media are a huge problem in that sense, as Ari said, because one of the mechanisms to cultivate extremism, as we describe in the book,
sentences.zh: 我认为社交媒体在这方面是一个巨大的问题，正如阿里所说，因为正如我们在书中描述的那样，培养极端主义的机制之一就是……

sentences.en: is what in psychology is known as mere exposure.
sentences.zh: 就是心理学中所说的“单纯曝光效应”。

sentences.en: So this is a very well-known psychological phenomenon that a person who goes on his morning run, if that person sees an observer casually looking over, they will run faster.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常著名的心理学现象：一个人在晨跑时，如果发现有旁观者在随意打量，他们会跑得更快。

sentences.en: So they will expand more energy.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会消耗更多的能量。

sentences.en: They will become a little more extreme in whatever it is that they're doing.
sentences.zh: 无论他们在做什么，都会表现得更加极端一些。

sentences.en: So this idea that you're being judged by others is a natural ingredient that helps extremism thrive.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种“被他人评判”的想法，是助长极端主义滋生的天然养分。

sentences.en: And even before, we were judged by our friends and neighbors.
sentences.zh: 甚至在过去，我们也会受到朋友和邻居的评判。

sentences.en: Now, it seems like the whole world is looking when we're posting or commenting or liking.
sentences.zh: 而现在，当我们发布内容、评论或点赞时，似乎全世界都在注视着我们。

sentences.en: So we're on the stage, and not in a good way, you know, and that makes extremism grow.
sentences.zh: 我们就像站在舞台上，而且不是以一种好的方式，你知道的，这促使了极端主义的增长。

sentences.en: But also another thing that is relevant here is COVID, which was an existential crisis, especially in the beginning when we didn't know much about the virus.
sentences.zh: 此外，还有一个与之相关的问题，那就是新冠疫情。这是一场生存危机，尤其是在我们对病毒知之甚少的初期。

sentences.en: It looked horrible.
sentences.zh: 当时看起来太可怕了。

sentences.en: And as I already said, crisis is one thing for which extremism is built.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前所说，危机是极端主义赖以生存的土壤之一。

sentences.en: And so around the world, we saw huge political changes take place after COVID, including protests.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们在全球范围内看到新冠疫情后发生了巨大的政治变革，包括抗议活动。

sentences.en: We had Black Lives Matter protests here, and then we had the January 6th protests, and we had populist movements come into power in a lot of countries.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有“黑人的命也是命”抗议活动，随后是1月6日的抗议活动，许多国家的民粹主义运动也纷纷上台。

sentences.en: We've all become a little more extreme, and I think we're still going through it from where I'm sitting.
sentences.zh: 我们都变得更加极端了一些，而且在我看来，我们目前仍处于这一过程中。

sentences.en: Do political extremists tend to fall on one side of the spectrum or the other, or are they evenly distributed?
sentences.zh: 政治极端分子倾向于处于光谱的一侧还是另一侧，还是说他们分布均匀？

sentences.en: I would say that they can be evenly distributed.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们是可以均匀分布的。

sentences.en: We have had waves of left-wing extremism culminating in communism that took over large portions of the world.
sentences.zh: 我们曾经历过左翼极端主义的浪潮，最终导致共产主义接管了世界上的大部分地区。

sentences.en: And we, of course, had fascism and Nazism that also threatened the security and stability of the planet.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们也经历过法西斯主义和纳粹主义，它们同样威胁着地球的安全与稳定。

sentences.en: Now we have right-wing rising nationalism, rising religious extremism.
sentences.zh: 现在我们又面临右翼民族主义的抬头和宗教极端主义的兴起。

sentences.en: And so the ideologies, the narratives that can serve extremism can vary in content.
sentences.zh: 因此，服务于极端主义的意识形态和叙事，其内容可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: The important thing is that they are presented as something that serves this all-important need to matter, to be significant.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，它们被呈现为一种能够满足“重要性需求”的东西，即渴望被重视、渴望有意义。

sentences.en: Who creates these narratives?
sentences.zh: 是谁创造了这些叙事？

sentences.en: Does the leading extremist sort of start the ball rolling?
sentences.zh: 是领头的极端分子开启了这一切吗？

sentences.en: And it sounds like there is a level of contagion, social contagion going on here.
sentences.zh: 听起来这里存在一种传染，一种社会传染。

sentences.en: Am I getting that right?
sentences.zh: 我理解得对吗？

sentences.en: It's an interesting question that I've been asked a lot with respect to QAnon in particular,
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的问题，关于“匿名者Q”（QAnon），我经常被问到这个问题，

sentences.en: which was on the front pages of newspapers in this country for a few years, and I've studied it some.
sentences.zh: 它在过去几年里曾登上这个国家报纸的头版，我也对此做过一些研究。

sentences.en: And a lot of people were interested in who is behind it.
sentences.zh: 很多人都对幕后推手是谁感兴趣。

sentences.en: And in fact, there were a couple of documentaries that were done by HBO and some other authoritative resources.
sentences.zh: 事实上，HBO和其他一些权威资源也制作过几部纪录片。

sentences.en: But I think it's less interesting who creates it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，谁创造了它并不那么重要。

sentences.en: And one reason is that none of these narratives are new.
sentences.zh: 原因之一是，这些叙事都不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: So with respect to QAnon, every single conspiracy theory that is embraced by QAnon has been around for decades, if not sometimes centuries or millennia, whether it's blood libel,
sentences.zh: 就“匿名者Q”而言，它所信奉的每一个阴谋论都已经存在了几十年，甚至有时是几个世纪或几千年，无论是“血祭诽谤”，

sentences.en: people drinking blood of children, or it's flat earth, or it's, you know, human-lizard hybrids who were going to take over the world.
sentences.zh: 还是人们喝儿童的血，或者是“地平说”，又或者是那些即将接管世界的“人蜥混血儿”。

sentences.en: All of those we've known, they've been around, it's like viruses are in the air all the time.
sentences.zh: 所有这些我们都知道，它们一直存在，就像病毒一样，时刻充斥在空气中。

sentences.en: And it's only when the immune system is weakened or compromised that we become susceptible to these viral stories and allow them to colonize and threaten our society.
sentences.zh: 只有当免疫系统减弱或受损时，我们才会容易受到这些病毒式故事的感染，并允许它们殖民我们的思想，威胁我们的社会。

sentences.en: And in fact, if you look through the history at the time when these conspiratorial narratives became dangerous and deadly and resulted in a huge number of deaths, like,
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你回顾历史，看看那些阴谋论叙事变得危险、致命并导致大量死亡的时期，比如，

sentences.en: for example, the witch hunts did, or like, for example, the Protocols of the Elders of Zion did.
sentences.zh: 猎巫运动，或者《锡安长老会纪要》所带来的后果。

sentences.en: Each of those resulted in thousands, if not tens of thousands of people being killed or tortured or otherwise really, you know, treated horribly for no good reason at all.
sentences.zh: 每一次都导致成千上万的人被杀害、折磨，或者仅仅因为毫无根据的理由而受到极其恶劣的对待。

sentences.en: In both of those cases, the narratives have long predated their rise to the surface as this major phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下，这些叙事在作为重大现象浮出水面之前，就已经存在很久了。

sentences.en: And in both of those cases, they were very quickly discovered to be a fraud.
sentences.zh: 而且在这两种情况下，它们很快就被发现是骗局。

sentences.en: It was known at the time of witch hunts that the book was a fraud.
sentences.zh: 在猎巫运动时期，人们就知道那本书是骗局。

sentences.en: It was known at the time of Protocols of the Elders of Zion that the book was a fraud.
sentences.zh: 在《锡安长老会纪要》时期，人们也知道那本书是骗局。

sentences.en: Just as it was known at the time of QAnon that it was a completely debunked conspiracy theory.
sentences.zh: 就像在“匿名者Q”时期，人们也知道它是一个被彻底揭穿的阴谋论一样。

sentences.en: And that doesn't stop it from spreading and it doesn't stop it from affecting people and it doesn't stop them from engaging in extreme behaviors like spending days and nights online in these rabbit holes of conspiracy theories and neglecting their own families.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能阻止它的传播，不能阻止它影响人们，也不能阻止人们参与极端行为，比如没日没夜地沉溺于这些阴谋论的“兔子洞”中，而忽略了自己的家庭。

sentences.en: And in fact, breaking up relationships with their siblings, with their spouses, their children over these beliefs.
sentences.zh: 事实上，甚至因为这些信仰而与兄弟姐妹、配偶、子女断绝关系。

sentences.en: And in some really extreme cases, people will kill their children.
sentences.zh: 在一些极端情况下，人们甚至会杀害自己的孩子。

sentences.en: We've had these incidents happen where they believe that the children are human lizard hybrids or they believe that the children are destined for the cabal.
sentences.zh: 我们曾发生过这样的事件：他们相信孩子是人蜥混血儿，或者相信孩子注定要被邪恶集团利用。

sentences.en: And so it's better that they be murdered at the hand of their mother.
sentences.zh: 所以，死在母亲手里反而更好。

sentences.en: So the ideology itself is just kind of a veneer on the real problem, which is that people feel that they're living in a time of crisis and that their existence is threatened.
sentences.zh: 因此，意识形态本身只是掩盖真正问题的一层外衣，真正的问题是人们感到自己生活在危机时代，生存受到了威胁。

sentences.en: And unless they do something extreme, all will be lost, which is what is a common thread among all of these different historical cases.
sentences.zh: 除非他们采取极端行动，否则一切都将失去，这是所有这些历史案例中的共同点。

sentences.en: So, you know, they say that the professional psychology is desperately trying to catch with common sense.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，人们常说专业心理学正拼命追赶常识。

sentences.en: And, you know, there is a sense in which people know psychology, they know the vulnerabilities, they know the threats,
sentences.zh: 而且，在某种意义上，人们了解心理学，了解脆弱性，了解威胁，

sentences.en: they know how to push people's buttons and what kind of story to tell them to mobilize them to extreme actions.
sentences.zh: 他们知道如何触动人们的痛点，知道该讲什么样的故事来动员他们采取极端行动。

sentences.en: Stories about, you know, children being killed, women being raped, things that threaten your masculinity and mobilize you to action.
sentences.zh: 关于儿童被杀、妇女被强奸的故事，这些威胁到你男子气概并动员你采取行动的事情。

sentences.en: These things are known.
sentences.zh: 这些都是已知的。

sentences.en: We know it from our own psychology, from the psychology of our children, our friends.
sentences.zh: 我们从自己的心理、从孩子和朋友的心理中都能了解到这一点。

sentences.en: And, you know, people who want to rise to power or want to exert influence are using it in creative ways,
sentences.zh: 而且，想要掌权或施加影响的人正在以创造性的方式利用它，

sentences.en: capitalizing on stories and themes that existed for centuries in order to capture the moment,
sentences.zh: 利用几个世纪以来就存在的故事和主题，来抓住时机，

sentences.en: the point of vulnerability and the point of vulnerability and the MS power, MS influence and most votes ascend to political stations and so forth.
sentences.zh: 抓住脆弱点，利用这些脆弱点来获取权力、影响力，并获得选票，从而登上政治舞台等等。

sentences.en: For our listeners who might be concerned that either they themselves or someone they know is tending toward extremism.
sentences.zh: 对于那些可能担心自己或身边人正趋向极端主义的听众，

sentences.en: First of all, how do you know that you're reaching a danger point and what can you do to pull yourself away?
sentences.zh: 首先，你怎么知道自己正处于危险边缘？你可以做些什么来让自己抽身？

sentences.en: One red flag that is actually often described as such by people in the prevention of violent crime community
sentences.zh: 暴力犯罪预防社区的人们通常会将一个危险信号描述为：

sentences.en: is when the person starts pulling away from their social circles, when they all of a sudden stop going to meetings with people that they used to regularly see,
sentences.zh: 当一个人开始疏远社交圈时，当他们突然停止参加以前经常见面的聚会时，

sentences.en: when they end up spending more and more time alone or completely changed their social circle.
sentences.zh: 当他们最终花越来越多的时间独处，或者彻底改变了社交圈时。

sentences.en: So this social disconnect, as we've discussed before,
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我们之前讨论过的，这种社交脱节，

sentences.en: is often a hallmark of increasing extremism because the person has already done or said something that alerted people in their circle,
sentences.zh: 往往是极端主义加剧的标志，因为此人已经做过或说过某些事情，引起了圈内人的警觉，

sentences.en: that caused them to talk to the person or express their disagreement with the extremist position, causing a rift or a strain on the relationship.
sentences.zh: 导致他们与此人交谈或表达对极端立场的不满，从而造成了关系上的裂痕或紧张。

sentences.en: So when this isolation or a change of social milieu is in place, this is a hallmark of abutting extremism.
sentences.zh: 因此，当这种孤立或社交环境的改变出现时，这就是极端主义萌芽的标志。

sentences.en: So if your loved one is exhibiting something like that, then the best thing to do is to try to stay around.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你的亲人表现出类似的情况，最好的办法就是尽量陪伴在他们身边。

sentences.en: Instead of arguing with them, which is the natural thing to do, instead of trying to disabuse them of what you think are their mistaken motions,
sentences.zh: 不要试图与他们争论（这是人的本能反应），也不要试图去纠正你认为他们错误的观念，

sentences.en: try to be there for them on just a human level, not on the level of discussing politics or whatever extremism the person is leaning into, but trying to understand their feelings.
sentences.zh: 试着在人性的层面上陪伴他们，而不是讨论政治或他们所倾向的任何极端主义，而是试着去理解他们的感受。

sentences.en: What is it that makes them feel that they're living in a crisis?
sentences.zh: 是什么让他们觉得生活在危机之中？

sentences.en: What is it that makes them be willing to break social connections, be willing to sacrifice things and support them in a way that is genuine and kind and constant,
sentences.zh: 是什么让他们愿意打破社会联系，愿意牺牲一切？以一种真诚、友善且持续的方式支持他们，

sentences.en: which from research we know is the best bet to get a person out of extremist situations at a moment when they're ready to do so?
sentences.zh: 根据研究，我们知道这是在他们准备好时，帮助他们走出极端处境的最佳选择。

sentences.en: I wanted to add a couple of comments.
sentences.zh: 我想补充几点评论。

sentences.en: First of all, we must remember that extreme isn't necessarily a negative thing.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们必须记住，极端并不一定是一件负面的事情。

sentences.en: Some of the greatest contributions to science, to art, to political philosophy, to world peace, were contributed by people who are extremists.
sentences.zh: 科学、艺术、政治哲学和世界和平领域的一些最伟大的贡献，都是由极端分子做出的。

sentences.en: Martin Luther King used to refer to himself as a radical.
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金过去常称自己为激进分子。

sentences.en: So, you know, this focused commitment to a cause can be in the service of good things, of pro-social things, things that construct rather than distract.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种对事业的专注投入，可以服务于美好的事物，服务于亲社会的事物，服务于建设而非破坏的事物。

sentences.en: However, we also know that extremists take a toll on the extremists.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们也知道极端主义会给极端分子自身带来代价。

sentences.en: We recently carried out, our team carried out research on 70 nations, and the one robust finding is that extremism is negatively related to well-being.
sentences.zh: 我们最近对70个国家进行了研究，一个稳健的发现是，极端主义与幸福感呈负相关。

sentences.en: It takes a price.
sentences.zh: 它是有代价的。

sentences.en: The fact that you suppress your needs, suppress your social needs, suppress your family connections, suppress your relatedness, takes its toll.
sentences.zh: 你压抑自己的需求、压抑社交需求、压抑家庭联系、压抑人际关系，这些都会付出代价。

sentences.en: And at the end of the day, the extremists are not happy campers.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，极端分子并不快乐。

sentences.en: They suffer a lot.
sentences.zh: 他们承受着巨大的痛苦。

sentences.en: So that has to be taken into consideration.
sentences.zh: 所以这一点必须考虑在内。

sentences.en: And I think that the third thing is that psychological literacy, understanding yourself, understanding reading our book, if I may suggest that.
sentences.zh: 我认为第三点是心理素养，了解自己，了解自我，阅读我们的书，如果我能这样建议的话。

sentences.en: Sophia is supporting me in that recommendation.
sentences.zh: 索菲亚也支持我的这个建议。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Understanding, you know, your own psyche, understanding when too much is too much, and what you are actually doing in excluding everything else for this one crazy commitment,
sentences.zh: 了解你自己的心理，了解什么时候“过犹不及”，以及你为了这个疯狂的投入而排斥其他一切，这到底是在做什么，

sentences.en: that can give you pause and allow you to navigate, to regulate your life in a more judicious, thoughtful way.
sentences.zh: 这能让你停下来思考，让你以一种更审慎、更深思熟虑的方式去驾驭和调节你的生活。

sentences.en: So how did you each get interested in studying this syndrome, this situation?
sentences.zh: 那么你们每个人是如何对研究这种综合征、这种情况产生兴趣的呢？

sentences.en: We both come from the study of terrorism.
sentences.zh: 我们都来自恐怖主义研究领域。

sentences.en: And for me, the bulb was the time where the term terrorism was replaced by the term violent extremism.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，转折点是“恐怖主义”一词被“暴力极端主义”一词取代的时候。

sentences.en: And Sophia knows the background to that change.
sentences.zh: 索菲亚知道这一变化的背景。

sentences.en: I thought it's political correctness, but it's more than that.
sentences.zh: 我原以为这是政治正确，但其实远不止于此。

sentences.en: And when I pondered the term violent extremism, I realized that maybe there are other extremism that are not violent, extreme diets, extreme sports, extreme love crashes,
sentences.zh: 当我思考“暴力极端主义”这个词时，我意识到也许还有其他非暴力的极端主义，比如极端饮食、极限运动、极端的恋爱冲动，

sentences.en: all kinds of behavioral and substance addictions.
sentences.zh: 各种行为成瘾和物质成瘾。

sentences.en: These are all forms of extremism.
sentences.zh: 这些都是极端主义的形式。

sentences.en: And I pondered whether there could be a common psychological core to those various extremism.
sentences.zh: 我思考这些不同的极端主义是否有一个共同的心理核心。

sentences.en: And that's when we started talking about the possibility of this motivational imbalance when one need overrides everything else.
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时，我们开始讨论这种“动机失衡”的可能性，即当一种需求压倒一切时。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we both study terrorism, but I had, although I didn't yet think of it in terms of extremism,
sentences.zh: 我们都研究恐怖主义，但我当时虽然还没有从极端主义的角度去思考，

sentences.en: it was very clear to me that some of the greatest visionaries that our civilization is built around, including Jesus, right?
sentences.zh: 但我很清楚，我们文明所建立的基础中，一些最伟大的愿景家，包括耶稣，对吧？

sentences.en: They are extremists in fundamental ways.
sentences.zh: 他们在根本上都是极端分子。

sentences.en: Even if they reject violence, unlike terrorists, understanding the complete commitment that terrorists have
sentences.zh: 即使他们拒绝暴力，与恐怖分子不同，理解恐怖分子那种完全的投入，

sentences.en: helped me to understand self-sacrifice of people who have done fantastic things that we're all grateful for.
sentences.zh: 帮助我理解了那些做出伟大成就、让我们心存感激的人们的自我牺牲精神。

sentences.en: I mean, we enjoy, you know, rights and freedoms and technology and advances in medicine that were carried out by people who gave their all.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们享受着权利、自由、科技和医学进步，这些都是由那些倾其所有的人实现的。

sentences.en: People tested vaccines on themselves in the olden days.
sentences.zh: 在过去，人们在自己身上测试疫苗。

sentences.en: And a lot of doctors died as a result or suffered horrible consequences by doing this extreme self-sacrifice in the name of medicine
sentences.zh: 许多医生因此死亡，或者因为以医学之名进行这种极端的自我牺牲而遭受了可怕的后果，

sentences.en: or Maria Curie's extreme self-sacrifice in the name of her science.
sentences.zh: 或者像玛丽·居里以科学之名进行的极端自我牺牲。

sentences.en: I just want to be clear of something that we clarify in the book, but for the listeners too,
sentences.zh: 我只是想澄清一点，我们在书中也阐明了这一点，但对听众来说也一样，

sentences.en: that we don't believe, and we have examples in the book to support this, that it takes extremism to achieve great things.
sentences.zh: 我们并不认为——书中也有例子支持这一点——实现伟大成就必须依靠极端主义。

sentences.en: We don't believe that you must lay your life on the altar of science to advance it, or that nothing worth doing was ever done without huge personal sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 我们不认为你必须把生命放在科学的祭坛上才能推动它，也不认为没有巨大的个人牺牲就做不成任何有价值的事。

sentences.en: There are plenty of examples, including Einstein and others who lead, you know, Picasso, quite balanced lives,
sentences.zh: 有很多例子，包括爱因斯坦和其他人，比如毕加索，他们过着相当平衡的生活，

sentences.en: combining their deep, profound passion for either art or technology or science, whatever, with other interests,
sentences.zh: 将他们对艺术、技术或科学等方面的深厚热情，与其他兴趣结合起来，

sentences.en: be playing the violin or traveling the world or engaging with colleagues and friends and women, you know.
sentences.zh: 无论是拉小提琴、环游世界，还是与同事、朋友和女性交往，你知道的。

sentences.en: So it's not that extremism is a necessary component for our world to thrive, for our science to advance, for the human rights to flourish.
sentences.zh: 所以，极端主义并不是我们世界繁荣、科学进步、人权兴盛的必要组成部分。

sentences.en: It does sometimes help, but more often than not, it hurts, and it particularly hurts the people who engage in it.
sentences.zh: 它有时确实有帮助，但更多时候是有害的，尤其是对参与其中的人来说。

sentences.en: So last question.
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题。

sentences.en: I'd like to ask this one of most of the people I talk to.
sentences.zh: 我想问我交谈过的大多数人这个问题。

sentences.en: What are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 你们现在在研究什么？

sentences.en: What's next, either in this area or other areas where you are conducting research?
sentences.zh: 接下来要做什么，无论是在这个领域还是你们正在进行研究的其他领域？

sentences.en: We have a contract for a new book, and that book is going to be titled To Matter to Marvel.
sentences.zh: 我们已经签了一本新书的合同，书名暂定为《重要性与惊叹》。

sentences.en: And this attempts to juxtapose this human quest for significance and mattering with the opposite psychology of admiring, of belittling oneself in the vis-a-vis nature,
sentences.zh: 这本书试图将人类对意义和重要性的追求，与那种在自然面前、在更伟大的力量面前、在上帝面前、在伟大英雄面前那种赞叹、贬低自我的心理进行对比。

sentences.en: vis-a-vis greater forces, vis-a-vis God, vis-a-vis some great heroes.
sentences.zh: 这两者之间的平衡，对我们来说，代表了引导生活最健康的方式，

sentences.en: And the balance between these two that, again, to us represents the most healthy way of leading one's life,
sentences.zh: 既不执着于伟大，不进行过度的尝试，也不贬低自己到失去能动性的地步，

sentences.en: not being committed to greatness, to an excessive attempt, and not belittling oneself to the point of losing agency,
sentences.zh: 不失去自我感，而是能够既渺小又伟大，既存在又不存在，可以这么说。

sentences.en: losing a sense of self, but being able to be small and be big, to be and not to be, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说从极端主义转向中庸之道？

sentences.en: So moving from extremism to moderation, is that what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，是的。

sentences.en: To some extent, yes.
sentences.zh: 索菲亚，你想补充吗？

sentences.en: Would you like to add, Sophia?
sentences.zh: 我认为我们有这种需求，也许不是一种极端的需求，但我们都有需求，在日常生活中需要有某种比我们自身更伟大的东西可以去敬畏。

sentences.en: I think we have the need, maybe not an extreme need, but we all have a need to have something greater than ourselves that we can bow to in our daily lives.
sentences.zh: 对科学家来说可以是科学，对宗教人士来说可以是上帝，或者也可以是自然。

sentences.en: It can be science for scientists, or it can be God for people of religion, or it can be nature.
sentences.zh: 我们同时也需要感到重要，需要有意义。

sentences.en: And we also have the need to matter and to be significant.
sentences.zh: 而当这种深层的失衡出现时，我们就会陷入极端主义。

sentences.en: And when there is this deep imbalance is when we get extremism.
sentences.zh: 找到平衡点，获得那种宁静，同时满足“渺小”和“伟大”这两种需求，就是我们认为的美好生活。

sentences.en: And finding, threading the needle, finding that equanimity, satisfying both needs for being big and being small, is what we think is a good life.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢你们两位的到来。

sentences.en: Well, I want to thank you both for joining me.
sentences.zh: 这是一次非常迷人的对话。

sentences.en: This has been a very fascinating conversation.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我们。

sentences.en: Thank you for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我们。

sentences.en: Thank you for having us.
sentences.zh: 非常愉快。

sentences.en: It was delightful.

sentences.zh: 如果您喜欢您所听到的内容，请关注我们并留下评论。

sentences.en: And if you like what you've heard, please follow us and leave a review.
sentences.zh: 如果您对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，可以发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@apa.org。

sentences.zh: 《心理学谈话》由 Lee Weinerman 制作。

sentences.zh: 感谢您收听美国心理学会的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening for the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 我是 Kim Mills。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 再见。
